items.title: Regression target and chosen version
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real random variables on a probability
space, with $\mathbb E|Y|<\infty$, and choose a regular conditional law
$Q(x,dy)$ of $Y$ given $X=x$. On
$D=\{x:\int |y|\,Q(x,dy)<\infty\}$ define
$m(x)=\int y\,Q(x,dy)$, and put $m(x)=0$ off $D$. By
[[cor-conditional-expectation-as-a-measurable-function-of-the-conditioning-variable]],
$m$ is Borel measurable and $m(X)$ is a version of
$\mathbb E[Y\mid\sigma(X)]$. A **regression target** is the resulting
$P_X$-almost-sure equivalence class; a **chosen regression-function version**
is the particular Borel function selected by the specified conditional law.

Pointwise smoothness is an additional hypothesis on the chosen version. It is
not implied by existence of conditional expectation, and statements about
$m(x)$ at a specified point use that selected version.

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Nonparametric and Semiparametric Estimation, MIT course notes
Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Nearest Neighbors and Kernels

items.title: Local-linear moment matrix converges to a positive-definite limit
items.statement:
Let $X_i$ be iid real random variables with density $f$ continuous and
positive at a fixed point $x$. Let $K$ be finite-valued Borel, nonnegative,
symmetric, with $\int K=1$ and $0<\mu_2=\int u^2K(u)\,du<\infty$.
Assume compact kernel support, a globally bounded density $f$, or a bounded
rapid-tail kernel satisfying $\sup_{|u|\ge A}|u|^3K(u)\to0$.
For $h=h_n\to0$ with $nh_n\to\infty$, set $U_i=(x-X_i)/h_n$ and
$$M_n=\frac1{nh_n}\sum_{i=1}^nK(U_i)\begin{pmatrix}1\\U_i\end{pmatrix}(1,U_i).$$
Then
$$M_n\longrightarrow f(x)\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\mu_2\end{pmatrix}\quad\text{in probability},$$
and $\mathbb P(M_n\text{ is nonsingular})\to1$.
More generally, the proof establishes $(nh_n)^{-1}\sum_i L(U_i)\to f(x)\int L$
for any integrable Borel function $L$, if $f$ is bounded globally or $L$
has compact support. Boundedness or square integrability of $L$ is unnecessary.

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Nonparametric and Semiparametric Estimation, MIT course notes
Whitney K. Newey, Locally Linear Regression, MIT course notes

items.title: Nadaraya–Watson estimator
items.statement:
Assume AC as in [[def-regression-target-version]]. Fix a sample size $n\ge1$,
a prediction point $x\in\mathbb R$, a bandwidth $h>0$, a finite-valued
nonnegative Borel function $K:\mathbb R\to[0,\infty)$, and a fixed fallback
$a_0\in\mathbb R$. For data $(X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n$, put
$$D_{n,h}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n K((x-X_i)/h).$$
The **Nadaraya–Watson estimator** of the pointwise target $m(x)$ is
$$\widehat m_{\mathrm{NW},h}(x)= \begin{cases} \dfrac{\sum_{i=1}^n K((x-X_i)/h)Y_i}{D_{n,h}(x)},&D_{n,h}(x)>0,\\[6pt] a_0,&D_{n,h}(x)=0. \end{cases}$$
For fixed $x,h,n$, this is a Borel statistic on $(\mathbb R^2)^n$ with its
product Borel sigma-algebra: each weight, product, and finite sum is Borel;
the positive-denominator set is Borel, and division is continuous there. In
any statistical experiment on this sample space whose pointwise regression
estimand is $\psi_x(\theta)=m_\theta(x)$, with $m_\theta$ the selected
version from [[def-regression-target-version]], it is an estimator of
$\psi_x$ in the sense of [[def-statistic-and-estimator]]. The fallback is
part of the definition. Kernel regularity and bandwidth assumptions used for
bias or variance results are stated in those results.

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Nonparametric and Semiparametric Estimation, MIT course notes
Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Nearest Neighbors and Kernels

items.title: Pointwise squared-error risk for regression
items.statement:
Assume AC as used to select the regression version. Fix a statistical experiment indexed by $\theta$, a point $x$, a real
regression target $m_\theta(x)$, and a real-valued estimator
$T_x$ of that target, meaning a measurable statistic with target space
$\mathbb R$ as in [[def-statistic-and-estimator]]. At this point, use the
squared-error loss
$$L_x(\theta,a)=(a-m_\theta(x))^2,\qquad a\in\mathbb R.$$
Its **pointwise squared-error risk** is the possibly infinite quantity
$$R_x(\theta,T_x)=\int (T_x(z)-m_\theta(x))^2\,P_\theta(dz)\in[0,\infty].$$
This is the deterministic-rule specialization of the risk in
[[def-loss-function-and-risk]]: the action space is $\mathbb R$ with its
Borel sigma-algebra, the action is $T_x(z)$, and the loss section is
measurable because it is continuous in $a$. The integral is nonnegative, so
it is defined without a finite-moment assumption.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.1
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §§4.1–4.2

items.title: Local-polynomial estimator
items.statement:
Assume AC as in [[def-regression-target-version]]. Fix $n\ge1$, a point
$x\in\mathbb R$, bandwidth $h>0$, degree $p\in\mathbb N_0$, a finite-valued
nonnegative Borel function $K$, and fallback $a_0\in\mathbb R$. Set
$u_i=(x-X_i)/h$, $r_p(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\mathsf T$, let $Z$ be the matrix
whose $i$th row is $r_p(u_i)^\mathsf T$, let
$W=\operatorname{diag}(K(u_1),\ldots,K(u_n))$, and put
$M=Z^\mathsf TWZ$. If $M$ is nonsingular, define
$$\widehat\beta=M^{-1}Z^\mathsf TW(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n)^\mathsf T,\qquad \widehat m_{p,h}(x)=\widehat\beta_0.$$
If $M$ is singular, define $\widehat m_{p,h}(x)=a_0$. For fixed $x,h,n,p$
and Borel $K$, this is a real statistic on $(\mathbb R^2)^n$ with its product
Borel sigma-algebra: the matrix entries are Borel, the nonsingular-matrix set
is Borel, matrix inversion is continuous there, and the fixed fallback gives
the other branch. In any statistical experiment on this sample space whose
pointwise regression estimand is $\psi_x(\theta)=m_\theta(x)$, with
$m_\theta$ the selected version from [[def-regression-target-version]], it
estimates $\psi_x$ in the sense of [[def-statistic-and-estimator]]. The case
$p=1$ is the **local-linear estimator**. No claim that $M$ is nonsingular for
a given sample is implicit in this definition.

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Locally Linear Regression, MIT course notes
Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Nearest Neighbors and Kernels

items.title: Pointwise risk is variance plus squared bias
items.statement:
Assume AC as used to select the regression target version. Fix a model
parameter $\theta$ and point $x$. Let $T_x$ be a real estimator of the finite
target $\psi=m_\theta(x)$ with $\mathbb E_\theta[T_x^2]<\infty$. Define its
bias by $b_\theta(x)=\mathbb E_\theta[T_x]-m_\theta(x)$. Its pointwise
squared-error risk from [[def-pointwise-regression-risk]] satisfies
$$R_x(\theta,T_x)=\operatorname{Var}_\theta(T_x)+b_\theta(x)^2.$$

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.1
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §§4.1–4.2

items.title: Pointwise population bias of the Nadaraya–Watson smoother
items.statement:
Assume AC for the chosen regression version [[def-regression-target-version]].
Let $X$ have Lebesgue density $f$, with $f(x)>0$ at a fixed interior point
$x$, and let $f,m$ be $C^2$ near $x$. Let $K$ be a finite-valued Borel,
nonnegative, symmetric kernel with $\int K=1$,
$0<\mu_2=\int u^2K(u)\,du<\infty$ and $\int K^2<\infty$.
Assume either that $K$ has compact support, or that $f,m$ and their first
two derivatives are bounded and continuous on $\mathbb R$. In these first two alternatives, no continuity
or boundedness of $K$ is required. The global alternative supplies tail
control for noncompact kernels; local smoothness alone does not supply it.
A further localization alternative, including the Gaussian kernel, is that
$\mathbb E[Y^2]<\infty$, $K$ is bounded, and
$$\lim_{A\to\infty}\sup_{|u|\ge A}|u|^3K(u)=0.$$
Under this rapid-tail alternative only the stated local smoothness of
$f,m$ is needed; no global boundedness of $m$ or of its derivatives is assumed.
For sufficiently small $h>0$, the population smoother corresponding to
[[def-nadaraya-watson-estimator]] is well defined by
$$m_h(x)=\frac{\int K(u)m(x-hu)f(x-hu)\,du}{\int K(u)f(x-hu)\,du},$$
and
$$m_h(x)-m(x)=\frac{h^2\mu_2}{2}\left(m''(x)+2m'(x)\frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\right)+o(h^2).$$

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Nonparametric and Semiparametric Estimation, MIT course notes
Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Nearest Neighbors and Kernels

items.title: Pointwise population bias of local-linear regression
items.statement:
Assume AC for the chosen regression version [[def-regression-target-version]].
Let $X$ have density $f$, with $f(x)>0$ at a fixed interior point $x$,
and let $f,m$ be $C^2$ near $x$. Let $K$ be a finite-valued Borel,
nonnegative symmetric kernel with $\int K=1$,
$0<\mu_2=\int u^2K(u)\,du<\infty$ and $\int K^2<\infty$.
Assume either compact kernel support, or that $f,m$ and their first two
derivatives are bounded and continuous on $\mathbb R$.
A further localization alternative, including the Gaussian kernel, is that
$\mathbb E[Y^2]<\infty$, $K$ is bounded, and
$$\lim_{A\to\infty}\sup_{|u|\ge A}|u|^3K(u)=0.$$
Under this rapid-tail alternative only the stated local smoothness of
$f,m$ is needed; no global boundedness of $m$ or of its derivatives is assumed.
Set
$$S_j(h)=\int K(u)u^j f(x-hu)\,du,\qquad T_j(h)=\int K(u)u^j f(x-hu)m(x-hu)\,du.$$
For sufficiently small $h$, $D_h=S_0S_2-S_1^2>0$ and the population
local-linear intercept, in the coordinates of [[def-local-polynomial-estimator]], is
$$m_{\mathrm{LL},h}(x)=\frac{S_2T_0-S_1T_1}{D_h}.$$
Then
$$m_{\mathrm{LL},h}(x)-m(x)=\frac{h^2\mu_2}{2}m''(x)+o(h^2).$$
This requires no fourth kernel moment.

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Nonparametric and Semiparametric Estimation, MIT course notes
Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Nearest Neighbors and Kernels

items.title: Conditional-on-design bias of the empirical local-linear estimator
items.statement:
Assume AC for the chosen regression version. Let $X_i$ be iid with density
$f$, with $f(x)>0$ at a fixed interior point $x$, and let $f,m$ be $C^2$
near $x$. Let $K$ be finite-valued Borel, nonnegative and symmetric, with
$\int K=1$, $0<\mu_2=\int u^2K<\infty$ and
$\int(1+u^2)K(u)^2\,du<\infty$. Assume either compact kernel support, or
that $f,m$ and their first two derivatives are bounded and continuous
globally. A further localization alternative, including the Gaussian kernel, is that
$\mathbb E[Y^2]<\infty$, $K$ is bounded, and
$$\lim_{A\to\infty}\sup_{|u|\ge A}|u|^3K(u)=0.$$
Under this rapid-tail alternative only the stated local smoothness of
$f,m$ is needed; no global boundedness of $m$ or of its derivatives is assumed.
Let $h_n\to0$ with $nh_n^3\to\infty$. For almost every realized design,
integrate the degree-one fit of [[def-local-polynomial-estimator]] against
the independent response laws $\prod_iQ(X_i,dy_i)$; call the resulting
finite response-law mean $b_n(x)$, with the same fixed fallback on singular
designs. Then
$$b_n(x)-m(x)=\frac{h_n^2\mu_2}{2}m''(x)+o_P(h_n^2).$$
Here $Z_n=o_P(h_n^2)$ means $Z_n/h_n^2\to0$ in probability. This is a
conditional response-law mean statement; it neither assumes nor asserts
that the estimator has an unconditional Lebesgue expectation.

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Nonparametric and Semiparametric Estimation, MIT course notes
Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Nearest Neighbors and Kernels

items.title: Conditional asymptotic variance of Nadaraya–Watson and local-linear estimators
items.statement:
Assume AC for the chosen regression version. Let $X_i$ be independent and
identically distributed with density $f$ continuous and positive at an
interior point $x$. For the chosen conditional law $Q(t,dy)$ in
[[def-regression-target-version]], set
$\sigma^2(t)=\int (y-m(t))^2Q(t,dy)$ where finite. Conditional on the
predictor vector, assume the responses are independent, have means $m(X_i)$,
and have variances $\sigma^2(X_i)$, where $\sigma^2$ is finite and continuous
at $x$. Let $K$ be finite-valued Borel, nonnegative, symmetric, with $\int K=1$,
$0<\mu_2=\int u^2K(u)\,du<\infty$ and $R(K)=\int K^2<\infty$.
Assume compact kernel support, globally bounded $f,\sigma^2$, or the
rapid-tail alternative: $\mathbb E Y^2<\infty$, bounded $K$, and
$\sup_{|u|\ge A}|u|^3K(u)\to0$. In this last alternative the stated
local continuity is sufficient.
For the local-linear conclusion also assume $\int u^2K(u)^2\,du<\infty$;
this extra squared moment is automatic for compactly supported kernels.
The Nadaraya–Watson conclusion requires only $R(K)<\infty$. For $h_n\to0$ with $nh_n\to\infty$, use the fixed
fallbacks in [[def-nadaraya-watson-estimator]] and
[[def-local-polynomial-estimator]]. Then, with variance taken conditionally
on $X_1,\ldots,X_n$,
$$nh_n\operatorname{Var}(\widehat m_{\mathrm{NW},h_n}(x)\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n) \longrightarrow \frac{R(K)\sigma^2(x)}{f(x)} \quad\text{in probability},$$
and the same limit holds with $\widehat m_{\mathrm{NW},h_n}(x)$ replaced by
the degree-one local-linear estimator. This is a conditional-variance
statement for both estimators. If additionally $m$ is continuous at $x$
and bounded globally (only bounded near $x$ is required for compact $K$),
or if the rapid-tail alternative holds and $m$ is continuous at $x$,
with $nh_n^3\to\infty$ additionally in this rapid-tail unconditional clause,
then the Nadaraya–Watson estimator is square-integrable for large $n$ and
$$\operatorname{Var}(\widehat m_{\mathrm{NW},h_n}(x))=\frac{R(K)\sigma^2(x)}{nh_nf(x)}+o((nh_n)^{-1}).$$
No unconditional local-linear variance is asserted: near-singular designs
can make even its finite-sample expectation undefined.

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Nonparametric and Semiparametric Estimation, MIT course notes
Whitney K. Newey, Locally Linear Regression, MIT course notes
Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Nearest Neighbors and Kernels

items.title: Finite-sample mean bias of the Nadaraya–Watson estimator
items.statement:
Assume AC for the chosen regression version. Let $X_i$ be iid with density
$f$, and, conditional on the predictors, let the responses be independent
with the selected conditional laws $Q(X_i,dy)$, means $m(X_i)$ and variances
$\sigma^2(X_i)$. At a fixed interior point $x$, suppose $f(x)>0$, $f,m$ are
$C^2$ near $x$, and $\sigma^2$ is finite and continuous at $x$.
Let $K$ be finite-valued Borel, nonnegative, symmetric, positive on some
neighborhood of zero, with $\int K=1$, $0<\mu_2=\int u^2K<\infty$ and
$R(K)=\int K^2<\infty$. Assume either compact kernel support, or that
$f,m$ and their first two derivatives are bounded and continuous globally
and $\sigma^2$ is finite and bounded globally. A further localization alternative, including the Gaussian kernel, is that
$\mathbb E[Y^2]<\infty$, $K$ is bounded, and
$$\lim_{A\to\infty}\sup_{|u|\ge A}|u|^3K(u)=0.$$
Under this rapid-tail alternative only the stated local smoothness of
$f,m$ is needed; no global boundedness of $m$ or of its derivatives is assumed.
For $h_n\to0$ with
$nh_n^3\to\infty$, and any fixed finite fallback, the estimator in
[[def-nadaraya-watson-estimator]] is integrable for all sufficiently large
$n$ and
$$\mathbb E[\widehat m_{\mathrm{NW},h_n}(x)]-m(x)=\frac{h_n^2\mu_2}{2}\left(m''(x)+2m'(x)\frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\right)+o(h_n^2).$$
The compact/global alternatives require no boundedness or continuity of $K$.

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Nonparametric and Semiparametric Estimation, MIT course notes
Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Nearest Neighbors and Kernels

items.title: Local-linear regression reproduces affine responses
items.statement:
Assume AC as in [[def-regression-target-version]]. Let $X,Y$ be real random
variables with $\mathbb E|Y|<\infty$ and $Y=a+bX$ almost surely. Choose the
regular conditional law $Q(t,dy)=\delta_{a+bt}(dy)$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$;
then the chosen regression-function version is $m(t)=a+bt$ at every point.
For any observed sample and any $x,h$ whose degree-one local moment matrix is
nonsingular, the local-linear estimate equals $a+bx$, even when the design
points are asymmetric around $x$.

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Locally Linear Regression, MIT course notes
Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Nearest Neighbors and Kernels

items.title: Local-linear estimator can lack a finite-sample expectation
items.statement:
At a fixed one-dimensional interior point, suppose the design density is
positive and $C^2$ locally, the chosen regression function is $C^2$ locally,
and the conditional response variance is finite and continuous. Suppose
$K$ is nonnegative, symmetric, positive near zero, normalized, with finite
positive second moment and finite squared integral. If $h_n\to0$,
$nh_n\to\infty$ and $nh_n^3\to\infty$, then the empirical local-linear fit
with a fixed fallback only on singular designs has a Lebesgue expectation
(and hence an unconditional second-order mean-bias expansion).

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Locally Linear Regression, MIT course notes
Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Nearest Neighbors and Kernels

items.title: Nadaraya–Watson bias from design gradients and boundaries
items.statement:
Symmetry of the kernel alone makes the population Nadaraya–Watson smoother
reproduce every affine regression function exactly in the interior and keeps
its bias of order $h^2$ at a support boundary.

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Nonparametric and Semiparametric Estimation, MIT course notes
Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Nearest Neighbors and Kernels
